NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A teen wants to carve the family histories on bark so they are not lost: record them all, or only what each family allows.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has noticed that the elders are getting old, and their stories are going with them. (subject.He/she) wants to carve them all on bark. Some elders love the idea. (friend) says some stories belong to a family, and are not for strangers to read. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) records every story (subject.he/she) can get. Most families are pleased. One family finds their private story carved and shown at the gathering, and is hurt. (subject) takes that bark back, and learns to ask first.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks each family what may be carved and what must stay spoken. It takes a long time. The bark records have gaps in them, and (subject) marks each gap with a small carved shell: a story that is kept, not lost.
